summary: The packet defines strong fail-closed scanning, artifact validation, verification, and framework boundaries, but two execution paths materially violate their documented trust model by forwarding unapproved ambient configuration or credentials into subprocesses.

findings.title: Approved command inherits unapproved ambient environment
findings.evidence: The publisher starts the target-controlled command with subprocess.Popen(command) and supplies no explicit env, so the complete parent environment—including credentials and injection variables—is inherited despite the debugger contract requiring approval of the exact command and its environment. The Cypress publisher uses the same pattern.
findings.recommendation: Execute target commands with an explicit minimal environment assembled from variables individually disclosed and approved by the user; reject undeclared environment forwarding.

findings.title: Pinned ast-grep download remains controlled by ambient npm configuration
findings.evidence: The optional npx-backed Tier 2 command is executed directly without a clean environment or trusted working directory. Consequently inherited npm_config variables and a target-repository .npmrc can select a registry or otherwise alter resolution, so pinning @ast-grep/cli@0.39.7 does not ensure the documented public third-party package boundary.
findings.recommendation: Run the npx fallback from private scanner storage with env -i, a fixed trusted registry, npm_config_userconfig=/dev/null, and no project-local npm configuration; otherwise fail closed.

limitations: Packet-only static review; no commands, tests, scanners, benchmarks, holdouts, repository history, or network checks were run.
The curated subset omits full product surfaces and cannot establish runtime success, detection accuracy, artifact integrity, or remote attestation.
